## Purpose and Scope

The Network Planning and Mapping system in OpenFE provides tools for creating, manipulating, and analyzing networks of small molecules with atom-to-atom mappings between them. These networks serve as the foundation for alchemical free energy calculations by defining which molecular transformations will be performed.

This page provides an overview of the network planning and mapping components in OpenFE. For detailed information about specific aspects, see [Atom Mapping](#3.1), [Ligand Networks](#3.2), and [Alchemical Network Planning](#3.3).

Sources: [openfe/setup/__init__.py:5-14](), [openfe/setup/ligand_network_planning.py:1-20]()

## Key Components

The network planning and mapping system consists of several interconnected components. OpenFE delegates the core network generation algorithms to the `konnektor` library, which provides specialized network planner classes.

```mermaid
graph TD
    AM["AtomMapper / LigandAtomMapper"] --> |"creates"| LAM["LigandAtomMapping"]
    LAM --> |"forms edges in"| LN["LigandNetwork"]
    LN --> |"used by"| ANP["AlchemicalNetworkPlanner"]
    SMC["SmallMoleculeComponent"] --> |"forms nodes in"| LN
    ANP --> |"generates"| ALE["Alchemical Transformations"]
    
    Konnektor["konnektor.network_planners"] --> |"provides"| StarGen["StarNetworkGenerator"]
    Konnektor --> |"provides"| MaxGen["MaximalNetworkGenerator"]
    Konnektor --> |"provides"| MSTGen["MinimalSpanningTreeNetworkGenerator"]
    Konnektor --> |"provides"| RedMSTGen["RedundantMinimalSpanningTreeNetworkGenerator"]
    
    StarGen --> |"generates"| LN
    MaxGen --> |"generates"| LN
    MSTGen --> |"generates"| LN
    RedMSTGen --> |"generates"| LN
```

**Diagram: Network Planning and Mapping Components with Konnektor Integration**

Sources: [openfe/setup/ligand_network_planning.py:1-24](), [openfe/setup/__init__.py:1-10]()

### Atom Mappers

Atom mappers determine how atoms in one molecule correspond to atoms in another molecule. This mapping defines which atoms will be transformed during an alchemical calculation. OpenFE provides several implementations through the `LigandAtomMapper` abstract base class:

| Mapper Class | Source | Algorithm | Key Parameters |
|--------------|--------|-----------|----------------|
| `LigandAtomMapper` | [openfe/setup/atom_mapping/ligandatommapper.py:11-66]() | Abstract base class | Must implement `_mappings_generator()` |
| `LomapAtomMapper` | [openfe/setup/atom_mapping/lomap_mapper.py:9]() | LOMAP MCS algorithm | `time`, `threed`, `element_change`, `seed` |
| `PersesAtomMapper` | [openfe/setup/atom_mapping/perses_mapper.py:25-111]() | Perses atom mapping | `allow_ring_breaking`, `preserve_chirality`, `use_positions`, `coordinate_tolerance` |
| `KartografAtomMapper` | [openfe/setup/atom_mapping/__init__.py:6]() | Kartograf algorithm | `atom_max_distance`, `atom_map_hydrogens`, `map_exact_ring_matches_only` |

Atom mappers implement the `_mappings_generator()` method ([openfe/setup/atom_mapping/ligandatommapper.py:20-38]()) which yields dictionaries of atom index mappings. These are wrapped into `LigandAtomMapping` objects by the `suggest_mappings()` method ([openfe/setup/atom_mapping/ligandatommapper.py:40-66]()).

Sources: [openfe/setup/atom_mapping/__init__.py:1-10](), [openfe/setup/atom_mapping/ligandatommapper.py:11-66](), [openfe/setup/atom_mapping/perses_mapper.py:25-111]()

### Ligand Networks

A `LigandNetwork` organizes multiple small molecules (represented as `SmallMoleculeComponent` objects) and the mappings between them. The network structure is a graph where:

- Nodes are `SmallMoleculeComponent` objects representing individual molecules
- Edges are `LigandAtomMapping` objects representing atom mappings between molecules

The network defines which transformations are possible and provides a framework for planning alchemical calculations.

Sources: [openfe/setup/__init__.py:11](), [openfe/tests/utils/conftest.py:13-19]()

### Alchemical Network Planners

Alchemical network planners use ligand networks to create plans for alchemical free energy calculations. OpenFE provides two main implementations:

- `RBFEAlchemicalNetworkPlanner`: For relative binding free energy calculations
- `RHFEAlchemicalNetworkPlanner`: For relative hydration free energy calculations

These planners generate a series of alchemical transformations based on the ligand network structure.

Sources: [openfe/setup/__init__.py:14]()

## Network Generation Strategies

OpenFE provides several strategies for generating ligand networks, each with different topological properties. These functions are implemented in `ligand_network_planning.py` and delegate to `konnektor.network_planners` classes for the actual network generation.

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "OpenFE API Functions"
        R["generate_radial_network()"]
        M["generate_maximal_network()"]
        MSN["generate_minimal_spanning_network()"]
        MRN["generate_minimal_redundant_network()"]
        CF["generate_network_from_names()"]
        CI["generate_network_from_indices()"]
    end

    subgraph "Konnektor Generators"
        StarGen["StarNetworkGenerator"]
        MaxGen["MaximalNetworkGenerator"]
        MSTGen["MinimalSpanningTreeNetworkGenerator"]
        RedMSTGen["RedundantMinimalSpanningTreeNetworkGenerator"]
        ExpGen["ExplicitNetworkGenerator"]
    end

    subgraph "Network Topologies"
        RSN["Radial/Star Network"]
        MN["Complete/Maximal Network"]
        MIN["Minimal Spanning Tree"]
        RN["Redundant MST"]
        CN["Custom Network"]
    end

    R --> StarGen --> RSN
    M --> MaxGen --> MN
    MSN --> MSTGen --> MIN
    MRN --> RedMSTGen --> RN
    CF --> ExpGen --> CN
    CI --> ExpGen --> CN

    AM["AtomMapper(s)"] --> R
    AM --> M
    AM --> MSN
    AM --> MRN
    AM --> CF
    AM --> CI

    Scorer["Scoring Function"] -.optional.-> R
    Scorer -.optional.-> M
    Scorer -.required.-> MSN
    Scorer -.required.-> MRN
```

**Diagram: Network Generation Strategies and Konnektor Integration**

| Function | Konnektor Class | Line Reference | Use Case |
|----------|----------------|----------------|----------|
| `generate_radial_network()` | `StarNetworkGenerator` | [openfe/setup/ligand_network_planning.py:49-154]() | All ligands to central hub |
| `generate_maximal_network()` | `MaximalNetworkGenerator` | [openfe/setup/ligand_network_planning.py:157-206]() | All possible pairs |
| `generate_minimal_spanning_network()` | `MinimalSpanningTreeNetworkGenerator` | [openfe/setup/ligand_network_planning.py:208-250]() | Minimum edges, maximum score |
| `generate_minimal_redundant_network()` | `RedundantMinimalSpanningTreeNetworkGenerator` | [openfe/setup/ligand_network_planning.py:252-304]() | Redundant paths for validation |
| `generate_network_from_names()` | `ExplicitNetworkGenerator` | [openfe/setup/ligand_network_planning.py:306-344]() | Custom specified edges |
| `generate_network_from_indices()` | `ExplicitNetworkGenerator` | [openfe/setup/ligand_network_planning.py:346-379]() | Custom specified edges |

Sources: [openfe/setup/ligand_network_planning.py:17-24](), [openfe/setup/ligand_network_planning.py:49-379]()

### Radial Networks

Radial networks (also known as hub-and-spoke or star networks) connect all ligands to a central reference ligand. This approach is useful when comparing multiple ligands to a common reference, such as a lead compound or a wild-type protein.

```python
network = generate_radial_network(
    ligands=ligands,
    central_ligand=central_ligand,
    mappers=mappers,
    scorer=optional_scorer,
    progress=False,
    n_processes=1
)
```

The `central_ligand` parameter can be:
- A `SmallMoleculeComponent` object
- A string matching a ligand's `name` attribute ([openfe/setup/ligand_network_planning.py:117-127]())
- An integer index into the `ligands` list ([openfe/setup/ligand_network_planning.py:109-116]())

Internally, this function creates a `StarNetworkGenerator` from konnektor ([openfe/setup/ligand_network_planning.py:130-139]()) and validates that all ligands are connected to the central hub ([openfe/setup/ligand_network_planning.py:141-153]()).

The function also applies the `_hasten_lomap()` optimization if using `LomapAtomMapper`, which pre-computes a common core to speed up subsequent mappings ([openfe/setup/ligand_network_planning.py:27-46]()).

Sources: [openfe/setup/ligand_network_planning.py:49-154]()

### Maximal Networks

Maximal networks attempt to create connections between all possible pairs of ligands. This provides comprehensive coverage but may include suboptimal transformations.

```python
network = generate_maximal_network(
    ligands=ligands,
    mappers=mappers,
    scorer=optional_scorer,
    progress=True
)
```

Sources: [openfe/setup/ligand_network_planning.py:141-200](), [openfe/tests/setup/test_network_planning.py:200-244]()

### Minimal Spanning Networks

Minimal spanning networks create a connected network with the minimum number of edges while maximizing the total score. This is the most common network topology for free energy calculations, as it provides complete connectivity with minimal computational cost.

```python
network = generate_minimal_spanning_network(
    ligands=ligands,
    mappers=mappers,
    scorer=scoring_function,  # Required for MST
    progress=True,
    n_processes=1
)
```

**Important:** The `scorer` parameter is required (not optional) for minimal spanning networks ([openfe/setup/ligand_network_planning.py:212]()). The scorer function must accept a `LigandAtomMapping` and return a `float`, where higher scores indicate better mappings. The algorithm selects edges to maximize the total network score while maintaining connectivity.

The function delegates to `MinimalSpanningTreeNetworkGenerator` from konnektor ([openfe/setup/ligand_network_planning.py:239-247]()).

Sources: [openfe/setup/ligand_network_planning.py:208-250]()

### Minimal Redundant Networks

Minimal redundant networks add redundancy to ensure each ligand is connected through multiple paths. This provides statistical validation through cycle closure and helps identify inconsistencies in free energy estimates.

```python
network = generate_minimal_redundant_network(
    ligands=ligands,
    mappers=mappers,
    scorer=scoring_function,  # Required
    progress=True,
    mst_num=2,  # Number of minimum spanning trees
    n_processes=1
)
```

The `mst_num` parameter controls the degree of redundancy ([openfe/setup/ligand_network_planning.py:279-283]()):
- `mst_num=2`: Each node connected by two edges (default)
- `mst_num=3`: Each node connected by three edges
- Higher values increase computational cost but improve cycle closure validation

The function delegates to `RedundantMinimalSpanningTreeNetworkGenerator` from konnektor ([openfe/setup/ligand_network_planning.py:293-301]()).

Sources: [openfe/setup/ligand_network_planning.py:252-304]()

### Custom Networks

Custom networks can be created by explicitly specifying connections between ligands. This is useful when domain knowledge suggests specific transformations or when replicating networks from other studies.

```python
# From molecule names
network = generate_network_from_names(
    ligands=ligands,
    mapper=mapper,
    names=[('benzene', 'toluene'), ('toluene', 'phenol')]
)

# From molecule indices
network = generate_network_from_indices(
    ligands=ligands,
    mapper=mapper,
    indices=[(0, 1), (1, 2)]
)
```

Both functions use `ExplicitNetworkGenerator` from konnektor ([openfe/setup/ligand_network_planning.py:339](), [openfe/setup/ligand_network_planning.py:376]()).

**Important validation:**
- `generate_network_from_names()` raises `KeyError` if a ligand name is not found ([openfe/setup/ligand_network_planning.py:331-332]())
- `generate_network_from_names()` raises `ValueError` if multiple ligands have the same name ([openfe/setup/ligand_network_planning.py:333-335]())
- `generate_network_from_indices()` raises `IndexError` if an index is out of bounds ([openfe/setup/ligand_network_planning.py:370-372]())

Sources: [openfe/setup/ligand_network_planning.py:306-379]()

## Integration with External Tools

OpenFE can import networks from other free energy calculation tools by parsing their network specification formats.

### Orion Networks

Networks can be imported from Orion Network Edge Specification (NES) format:

```python
network = load_orion_network(
    ligands=ligands,
    mapper=mapper,
    network_file='network.dat'
)
```

**File Format:** The Orion NES format uses the syntax `ligand1 >> ligand2` to specify edges, with comment lines starting with `#` ([openfe/setup/ligand_network_planning.py:407-411]()). Each edge should be on a separate line. Lines that don't match the expected format raise a `KeyError` ([openfe/setup/ligand_network_planning.py:415-417]()).

Sources: [openfe/setup/ligand_network_planning.py:381-425]()

### FEP+ Networks

Networks can be imported from Schrödinger's FEP+ edges format:

```python
network = load_fepplus_network(
    ligands=ligands,
    mapper=mapper,
    network_file='edges.edges'
)
```

**File Format:** The FEP+ format uses the syntax `hash:hash # name -> name` ([openfe/setup/ligand_network_planning.py:458-464]()). Each line must have exactly 5 space-separated fields. Lines that don't match this format raise a `KeyError` with a descriptive error message ([openfe/setup/ligand_network_planning.py:459-464]()).

Sources: [openfe/setup/ligand_network_planning.py:427-472]()

## CLI Integration and YAML Configuration

OpenFE provides CLI commands that integrate network planning into an automated workflow. The CLI uses YAML configuration files to specify mappers, network algorithms, and other options.

### CLI Commands

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "Input"
        SDF["Ligand SDF files"]
        PDB["Protein PDB file"]
        YAML["Settings YAML"]
    end

    subgraph "CLI Commands"
        PlanRBFE["plan-rbfe-network"]
        PlanRHFE["plan-rhfe-network"]
    end

    subgraph "Output"
        NetJSON["AlchemicalNetwork.json"]
        TransJSON["transformation_*.json files"]
        GraphML["ligand_network.graphml"]
    end

    SDF --> PlanRBFE
    PDB --> PlanRBFE
    YAML --> PlanRBFE
    
    SDF --> PlanRHFE
    YAML --> PlanRHFE

    PlanRBFE --> NetJSON
    PlanRBFE --> TransJSON
    PlanRBFE --> GraphML
    
    PlanRHFE --> NetJSON
    PlanRHFE --> TransJSON
    PlanRHFE --> GraphML
```

**Diagram: CLI Network Planning Commands**

The CLI commands are implemented in:
- **RBFE**: [openfecli/commands/plan_rbfe_network.py:120-256]()
- **RHFE**: [openfecli/commands/plan_rhfe_network.py:97-221]()

### YAML Configuration Structure

The YAML settings file allows customization of network planning without modifying code. The structure is parsed by [openfecli/parameters/plan_network_options.py:55-86]().

```yaml
mapper:
  method: KartografAtomMapper  # or LomapAtomMapper
  settings:
    atom_max_distance: 0.95
    atom_map_hydrogens: true

network:
  method: generate_minimal_spanning_network  # or others
  settings:
    # Network-specific parameters (e.g., mst_num for redundant networks)

partial_charge:
  method: am1bcc  # or nagl, espaloma, am1bccelf10
  settings:
    off_toolkit_backend: ambertools
```

**Mapper Choices** ([openfecli/parameters/plan_network_options.py:134-145]()):
- `"lomap"` or `"lomapatommapper"` → `LomapAtomMapper`
- `"kartograf"` or `"kartografatommapper"` → `KartografAtomMapper`

**Network Choices** ([openfecli/parameters/plan_network_options.py:162-177]()):
- `"generate_radial_network"` or `"radial"`
- `"generate_minimal_spanning_network"` or `"mst"` (default)
- `"generate_minimal_redundant_network"`
- `"generate_maximal_network"`
- `"generate_lomap_network"`

**Partial Charge Methods** ([openfecli/parameters/plan_network_options.py:182-190]()):
- `"am1bcc"`: AM1-BCC via AmberTools (default)
- `"am1bccelf10"`: AM1-BCC via OpenEye (requires license)
- `"nagl"`: Neural network charges via openff-nagl
- `"espaloma"`: Machine learning charges via espaloma

### Workflow Integration

The CLI commands automatically handle:

1. **Charge Assignment**: All molecules are automatically charged before network generation ([openfecli/commands/plan_rbfe_network.py:80-90](), [openfecli/commands/plan_rhfe_network.py:74-84]())
2. **Network Generation**: The specified algorithm generates the ligand network
3. **Alchemical Network Creation**: Protocol settings are applied to each transformation
4. **Output Serialization**: Networks and transformations are saved as JSON files ([openfecli/plan_alchemical_networks_utils.py:10-36]())

The output directory structure is:
```
alchemicalNetwork/
├── alchemicalNetwork.json
├── ligand_network.graphml
└── transformations/
    ├── rbfe_ligA_complex_ligB_complex.json
    ├── rbfe_ligA_solvent_ligB_solvent.json
    └── ...
```

Sources: [openfecli/commands/plan_rbfe_network.py:120-256](), [openfecli/commands/plan_rhfe_network.py:97-221](), [openfecli/parameters/plan_network_options.py:88-202]()

## Common Workflows

### Python API Workflow

```python
from openfe import SmallMoleculeComponent, LomapAtomMapper
from openfe.setup import ligand_network_planning, lomap_scorers

# 1. Load molecules
ligands = [
    SmallMoleculeComponent.from_sdf_file(f)
    for f in ligand_files
]

# 2. Choose mapper and scorer
mapper = LomapAtomMapper(time=20, threed=True)
scorer = lomap_scorers.default_lomap_score

# 3. Generate network
network = ligand_network_planning.generate_minimal_spanning_network(
    ligands=ligands,
    mappers=[mapper],
    scorer=scorer,
    progress=True
)

# 4. Use with alchemical planner
from openfe.setup import RBFEAlchemicalNetworkPlanner
from openfe.protocols import RelativeHybridTopologyProtocol

planner = RBFEAlchemicalNetworkPlanner(
    mappers=[mapper],
    mapping_scorer=scorer,
    ligand_network_planner=ligand_network_planning.generate_minimal_spanning_network,
    protocol=RelativeHybridTopologyProtocol.default_settings()
)

alchemical_network = planner(
    ligands=ligands,
    solvent=solvent,
    protein=protein
)
```

### CLI Workflow

```bash
# 1. Create settings YAML (optional, uses defaults otherwise)
cat > settings.yaml << EOF
mapper:
  method: KartografAtomMapper
  settings:
    atom_max_distance: 0.95

network:
  method: generate_minimal_spanning_network
EOF

# 2. Plan RBFE network
openfecli plan-rbfe-network \
    --molecules ligands/ \
    --protein protein.pdb \
    --settings settings.yaml \
    --output-dir my_network

# 3. Run transformations
openfecli quickrun \
    my_network/transformations/rbfe_ligA_complex_ligB_complex.json \
    --output results/

# 4. Gather results
openfecli gather results/ --report ddg
```

Sources: [openfecli/commands/plan_rbfe_network.py:19-117](), [openfecli/commands/plan_rhfe_network.py:21-94]()

## Scoring Functions and Mapper Optimization

Atom mapping quality can be improved using scoring functions that evaluate mappings. Scoring functions must be callables that accept a `LigandAtomMapping` and return a `float`, where higher values indicate better mappings.

### Predefined Scoring Functions

OpenFE provides scoring functions through two modules:

**LOMAP Scorers** ([openfe/setup/atom_mapping/lomap_scorers.py:1-17]()):
- `default_lomap_score`: Default LOMAP scoring algorithm
- `atomic_number_score`: Penalizes atomic number changes
- `ecr_score`: Electron-withdrawing group score
- `mcsr_score`: Maximum common subgraph ring score
- `mncar_score`: Minimum number of changed atoms in rings
- `tmcsr_score`: Transmuting maximum common subgraph rings
- `hybridization_score`: Penalizes hybridization changes
- `sulfonamides_score`: Sulfonamide-specific scoring
- `heterocycles_score`: Heterocycle-specific scoring
- `transmuting_methyl_into_ring_score`: Methyl to ring penalties
- `transmuting_ring_sizes_score`: Ring size change penalties

**Perses Scorers** ([openfe/setup/atom_mapping/perses_scorers.py:38-122]()):
- `default_perses_scorer`: Default Perses scoring with optional normalization
  - Supports `use_positions` for position-based scoring
  - Supports `normalize` to enable comparison across different molecule pairs

### Custom Scoring Functions

```python
def custom_scorer(mapping: LigandAtomMapping) -> float:
    """Example: Prefer mappings with more atoms mapped"""
    return len(mapping.componentA_to_componentB)

network = generate_minimal_spanning_network(
    ligands=ligands,
    mappers=[mapper1, mapper2],  # Multiple mappers
    scorer=custom_scorer
)
```

When multiple mappers are provided, each mapper generates candidate mappings, and the scorer selects the best mapping for each edge based on the highest score.

Sources: [openfe/setup/atom_mapping/lomap_scorers.py:1-17](), [openfe/setup/atom_mapping/perses_scorers.py:38-122]()

## Network Validation and Analysis

After generating a network, it's important to validate its properties:

- Connectivity: Ensure all nodes are reachable (`network.is_connected()`)
- Edge quality: Check mapping scores and atom count
- Network topology: Analyze the number of edges and their distribution

The `LigandNetwork` class provides methods for extracting and analyzing this information.

Sources: [openfe/tests/setup/test_network_planning.py:307-335]()

# Atom Mapping

Atom mapping is a core functionality in OpenFE that establishes correspondences between atoms in different molecules. This is a crucial step for alchemical free energy calculations where one molecule is transformed into another. The atom mapping system provides standardized interfaces for suggesting and evaluating mappings between small molecules.

For information about using atom mappings to construct networks of related molecules, see [Ligand Networks](#3.2). For planning alchemical transformations based on these mappings, see [Alchemical Network Planning](#3.3).

## Atom Mapping Overview

The atom mapping system identifies which atoms in one molecule correspond to which atoms in another molecule. These mappings are used to define the transformations that occur during alchemical simulations, where a molecule is gradually transformed into another.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph "Atom Mapping System"
        SMC1["SmallMoleculeComponent A"] --> Mapper["LigandAtomMapper"]
        SMC2["SmallMoleculeComponent B"] --> Mapper
        Mapper --> LAM["LigandAtomMapping"]
        Scorer["Mapping Scorer"] --> Score["Mapping Score"]
        LAM --> Scorer
    end

    LAM --> LN["LigandNetwork"]
    LN --> ANP["AlchemicalNetworkPlanner"]
    ANP --> Protocols["Simulation Protocols"]
```

Sources: [openfe/setup/atom_mapping/ligandatommapper.py:11-61](), [openfe/setup/atom_mapping/perses_mapper.py:26-108]()

## Atom Mapping Architecture

The atom mapping system is built around a few key classes:

1. `LigandAtomMapper` - Abstract base class defining the interface for all atom mappers
2. `LigandAtomMapping` - Class representing a specific mapping between two molecules
3. Concrete mapper implementations - `PersesAtomMapper`, `LomapAtomMapper`, `KartografAtomMapper`
4. Scoring functions - To evaluate mapping quality

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class gufe_AtomMapper {
        <<abstract>>
    }

    class LigandAtomMapper {
        <<abstract>>
        _mappings_generator(componentA, componentB)
        suggest_mappings(componentA, componentB)
    }

    class LigandAtomMapping {
        componentA: SmallMoleculeComponent
        componentB: SmallMoleculeComponent
        componentA_to_componentB: Dict[int, int]
        get_distances()
    }

    class PersesAtomMapper {
        allow_ring_breaking: bool
        preserve_chirality: bool
        use_positions: bool
        coordinate_tolerance: FloatQuantity
        _mappings_generator()
    }

    class LomapAtomMapper {
        time: int
        threed: bool
        max3d: float
        element_change: bool
        seed: str
        shift: bool
        _mappings_generator()
    }

    class KartografAtomMapper {
        _mappings_generator()
    }

    gufe_AtomMapper <|-- LigandAtomMapper
    LigandAtomMapper <|-- PersesAtomMapper
    LigandAtomMapper <|-- LomapAtomMapper  
    LigandAtomMapper <|-- KartografAtomMapper
    LigandAtomMapper ..> LigandAtomMapping : creates
```

Sources: [openfe/setup/atom_mapping/ligandatommapper.py:11-61](), [openfe/setup/atom_mapping/perses_mapper.py:26-108](), [openfe/setup/atom_mapping/__init__.py:1-10]()

## Available Atom Mappers

OpenFE provides multiple atom mapping implementations, each with different algorithms and characteristics:

### PersesAtomMapper

The `PersesAtomMapper` uses the Maximum Common Substructure (MCS) algorithm from the Perses package to suggest atom mappings between molecules.

```python
from openfe.setup.atom_mapping import PersesAtomMapper
from openff.units import unit

# Create a mapper with default settings
mapper = PersesAtomMapper()

# Or customize the behavior
mapper = PersesAtomMapper(
    allow_ring_breaking=False,
    preserve_chirality=True,
    use_positions=True,
    coordinate_tolerance=0.25 * unit.angstrom
)
```

Configuration options:
- `allow_ring_breaking` - Whether to allow mappings that break rings (default: True)
- `preserve_chirality` - Whether mappings must strictly preserve chirality (default: True)
- `use_positions` - Whether to use 3D coordinates in mapping (default: True)
- `coordinate_tolerance` - Tolerance for position-based mapping (default: 0.25 Å)

Sources: [openfe/setup/atom_mapping/perses_mapper.py:26-108]()

### LomapAtomMapper

The `LomapAtomMapper` uses the LOMAP (Lead Optimization Mapper) algorithm for atom mapping. This mapper is particularly suited for drug design applications.

```python
from openfe.setup.atom_mapping import LomapAtomMapper

# Create a mapper with default settings
mapper = LomapAtomMapper()

# Or customize the behavior
mapper = LomapAtomMapper(
    time=20,
    threed=True,
    max3d=1000.0,
    element_change=True,
    seed='',
    shift=True
)
```

Sources: [openfe/setup/atom_mapping/lomap_mapper.py:1-9](), [openfe/tests/setup/atom_mapping/test_lomap_atommapper.py:14-25]()

### KartografAtomMapper

The `KartografAtomMapper` leverages the Kartograf package for atom mapping.

```python
from openfe.setup.atom_mapping import KartografAtomMapper

# Create a mapper
mapper = KartografAtomMapper()
```

Sources: [openfe/setup/atom_mapping/__init__.py:6]()

## Using Atom Mappers

All atom mappers follow the same interface, making them interchangeable in most contexts:

```python
from openfe import SmallMoleculeComponent
from openfe.setup.atom_mapping import PersesAtomMapper

# Create two molecules
moleculeA = SmallMoleculeComponent(...)
moleculeB = SmallMoleculeComponent(...)

# Create a mapper
mapper = PersesAtomMapper()

# Get mappings (generator of LigandAtomMapping objects)
mappings_generator = mapper.suggest_mappings(moleculeA, moleculeB)

# Get the first mapping
try:
    mapping = next(mappings_generator)
    print(f"Found mapping with {len(mapping.componentA_to_componentB)} atoms mapped")
except StopIteration:
    print("No mapping found between molecules")
```

The `suggest_mappings` method returns a generator of `LigandAtomMapping` objects, each representing a possible mapping between the molecules. If no mappings are found, the generator will be empty.

Sources: [openfe/setup/atom_mapping/ligandatommapper.py:38-61](), [openfe/tests/setup/atom_mapping/test_perses_atommapper.py:11-38]()

## Mapping Scoring

OpenFE provides scoring functions to evaluate the quality of atom mappings. Different scoring approaches highlight different aspects of mapping quality.

### Perses Scorer

The Perses scorer evaluates mappings based on the number of mapped atoms and optionally their positions:

```python
from openfe.setup.atom_mapping import perses_scorers

# Score a mapping
score = perses_scorers.default_perses_scorer(
    mapping,
    use_positions=False,
    normalize=True
)
```

Sources: [openfe/setup/atom_mapping/perses_scorers.py:38-111]()

### LOMAP Scorers

LOMAP provides multiple scoring functions for different aspects of mapping quality:

```python
from openfe.setup.atom_mapping import lomap_scorers

# Default LOMAP score (combination of multiple criteria)
score = lomap_scorers.default_lomap_score(mapping)

# Individual scoring functions
mcsr_score = lomap_scorers.mcsr_score(mapping)  # Maximum Common Substructure Ratio
mncar_score = lomap_scorers.mncar_score(mapping)  # Maximum Number of Common Atoms Ratio
atomic_number_score = lomap_scorers.atomic_number_score(mapping)  # Atomic number matching
hybridization_score = lomap_scorers.hybridization_score(mapping)  # Hybridization state matching
sulfonamides_score = lomap_scorers.sulfonamides_score(mapping)  # Sulfonamide groups penalty
```

Sources: [openfe/setup/atom_mapping/lomap_scorers.py:1-17](), [openfe/tests/setup/atom_mapping/test_lomap_scorers.py:62-276]()

## LigandAtomMapping Structure

The `LigandAtomMapping` class represents a specific mapping between two molecules:

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class LigandAtomMapping {
        componentA: SmallMoleculeComponent
        componentB: SmallMoleculeComponent
        componentA_to_componentB: Dict[int, int]
        componentB_to_componentA: Dict[int, int]
        get_distances(): List[float]
    }
```

The mapping is represented as a dictionary where:
- Keys are atom indices in the first molecule (`componentA`)
- Values are corresponding atom indices in the second molecule (`componentB`)

The `get_distances` method calculates the 3D distances between mapped atoms, which can be useful for evaluating mapping quality.

Sources: [openfe/tests/setup/atom_mapping/test_lomap_atommapper.py:42-59](), [openfe/tests/utils/conftest.py:33-36]()

## Implementation Details

### LigandAtomMapper Base Class

The `LigandAtomMapper` is an abstract base class that defines the interface for all atom mappers:

```python
class LigandAtomMapper(gufe.AtomMapper):
    """
    Suggest atom mappings between two :class:`SmallMoleculeComponent` instances.

    Subclasses will typically implement the ``_mappings_generator`` method,
    which returns an iterable of :class:`.LigandAtomMapping` suggestions.
    """
    @abc.abstractmethod
    def _mappings_generator(self,
                            componentA: SmallMoleculeComponent,
                            componentB: SmallMoleculeComponent
                            ) -> Iterable[dict[int, int]]:
        """
        Suggest mapping options for the input molecules.

        Parameters
        ----------
        componentA, componentB : rdkit.Mol
            the two molecules to create a mapping for

        Returns
        -------
        Iterable[dict[int, int]] :
            an iterable over proposed mappings from componentA to componentB
        """
        ...

    def suggest_mappings(self, componentA: SmallMoleculeComponent,
                         componentB: SmallMoleculeComponent
    ) -> Iterable[LigandAtomMapping]:
        """
        Suggest :class:`.LigandAtomMapping` options for the input molecules.

        Parameters
        ---------
        componentA, componentB : :class:`.SmallMoleculeComponent`
            the two molecules to create a mapping for

        Returns
        -------
        Iterable[LigandAtomMapping] :
            an iterable over proposed mappings
        """
        for map_dct in self._mappings_generator(componentA, componentB):
            yield LigandAtomMapping(componentA, componentB, map_dct)
```

Concrete implementations need to provide the `_mappings_generator` method, which yields dictionaries mapping atom indices from the first molecule to the second. The base class takes care of wrapping these dictionaries in `LigandAtomMapping` objects.

Sources: [openfe/setup/atom_mapping/ligandatommapper.py:11-61]()

### PersesAtomMapper Implementation

The `PersesAtomMapper` uses the Perses package's Maximum Common Substructure algorithm:

```python
class PersesAtomMapper(LigandAtomMapper):
    def _mappings_generator(self, componentA, componentB):
        # Construct Perses Mapper
        _atom_mapper = AtomMapper(
            use_positions=self.use_positions,
            coordinate_tolerance=to_openmm(self.coordinate_tolerance),
            allow_ring_breaking=self.allow_ring_breaking)

        # Try generating a mapping
        try:
            _atom_mappings = _atom_mapper.get_all_mappings(
                    old_mol=componentA.to_openff(), new_mol=componentB.to_openff())
        except InvalidMappingException:
            return

        # Catch empty mappings here
        if _atom_mappings is None:
            return

        # Post processing
        if self.preserve_chirality:
            for x in _atom_mappings:
                x.preserve_chirality()

        # Translate mapping objects
        mapping_dict = (x.old_to_new_atom_map for x in _atom_mappings)

        yield from mapping_dict
```

The mapper converts the molecules to OpenFF format, uses the Perses mapper to generate mappings, and then yields each mapping.

Sources: [openfe/setup/atom_mapping/perses_mapper.py:82-108]()

## Integration with the OpenFE Workflow

Atom mapping is a key step in the OpenFE workflow for free energy calculations:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph "Chemical Input"
        SMC["Small Molecule Components"]
    end

    subgraph "Atom Mapping"
        AM["Atom Mappers:
        - PersesAtomMapper
        - LomapAtomMapper
        - KartografAtomMapper"]
        LAM["LigandAtomMapping"]
    end

    subgraph "Network Construction"
        LN["LigandNetwork"]
    end

    subgraph "Free Energy Calculations"
        ANP["AlchemicalNetworkPlanner"]
        Protocols["Simulation Protocols"]
    end

    SMC --> AM
    AM --> LAM
    LAM --> LN
    LN --> ANP
    ANP --> Protocols
```

1. The process starts with `SmallMoleculeComponent` objects representing the molecules of interest
2. Atom mappers identify corresponding atoms between molecules
3. These mappings are used to construct a `LigandNetwork` representing transformations between molecules
4. The `AlchemicalNetworkPlanner` uses this network to plan simulations
5. The planned simulations are executed using the appropriate simulation protocols

Sources: [openfe/tests/setup/atom_mapping/test_perses_atommapper.py:11-38](), [openfe/tests/utils/conftest.py:42-49]()

## Choosing an Atom Mapper

Different mappers have different strengths and are suitable for different types of transformations:

| Mapper | Strengths | Best for |
|--------|-----------|----------|
| PersesAtomMapper | Considers 3D structure, preserves chirality | Accurate mappings for similar molecules |
| LomapAtomMapper | Drug design specific rules, multiple scoring functions | Lead optimization in drug discovery |
| KartografAtomMapper | Modern algorithm with good performance | General purpose mappings |

When evaluating a specific mapper for your use case, consider:
1. The ability to find mappings for your molecules
2. The quality of mappings (use scoring functions)
3. Performance considerations for large sets of molecules

Sources: [openfe/setup/atom_mapping/perses_mapper.py:56-76](), [openfe/tests/setup/atom_mapping/test_lomap_atommapper.py:14-25]()

## Purpose and Scope

This page documents the `LigandNetwork` data structure and the various network topologies (radial, minimal spanning tree, maximal, redundant) available for organizing relative free energy calculations. A ligand network defines which pairs of ligands will be compared through alchemical transformations. Understanding network topology is critical for designing efficient, statistically robust free energy campaigns.

For information about atom mapping algorithms that determine *how* atoms are mapped within each edge, see [Atom Mapping](#3.1). For integration of networks with protocols to create `AlchemicalNetwork` objects, see [Alchemical Network Planning](#3.3).

---

## LigandNetwork Structure

A `LigandNetwork` is a directed graph where nodes are `SmallMoleculeComponent` instances and edges are `LigandAtomMapping` instances. The network represents a set of planned alchemical transformations.

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "LigandNetwork Components"
        Network["LigandNetwork<br/>(from gufe)"]
        Nodes["Nodes<br/>SmallMoleculeComponent<br/>instances"]
        Edges["Edges<br/>LigandAtomMapping<br/>instances"]
        Graph["Underlying Graph<br/>NetworkX DiGraph"]
    end
    
    Network --> Nodes
    Network --> Edges
    Network --> Graph
    
    subgraph "LigandAtomMapping Details"
        Mapping["LigandAtomMapping"]
        ComponentA["componentA<br/>SmallMoleculeComponent"]
        ComponentB["componentB<br/>SmallMoleculeComponent"]
        AtomMap["componentA_to_componentB<br/>dict[int, int]"]
        Annotations["annotations<br/>dict (optional scores)"]
    end
    
    Edges --> Mapping
    Mapping --> ComponentA
    Mapping --> ComponentB
    Mapping --> AtomMap
    Mapping --> Annotations
```

**Sources:** [openfe/setup/ligand_network_planning.py:1-26]()

### Key Properties

| Property | Type | Description |
|----------|------|-------------|
| `nodes` | `Iterable[SmallMoleculeComponent]` | All ligands in the network |
| `edges` | `Iterable[LigandAtomMapping]` | All mappings/transformations |
| `graph` | `networkx.DiGraph` | Underlying directed graph structure |

### Connectivity

Networks can be checked for connectivity using `network.is_connected()`. A connected network ensures all ligands can be related through some path of transformations, which is essential for computing relative binding free energies.

**Sources:** [openfe/setup/ligand_network_planning.py:49-154](), [openfe/tests/setup/test_network_planning.py:427]()

---

## Network Topology Types

OpenFE provides five primary strategies for generating ligand networks, each with distinct trade-offs between computational cost, statistical robustness, and result accuracy.

### Radial (Star) Network

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "Radial Network Topology"
        Central["Central Ligand<br/>(Hub)"]
        L1["Ligand 1"]
        L2["Ligand 2"]
        L3["Ligand 3"]
        L4["Ligand 4"]
        L5["Ligand 5"]
        
        Central --- L1
        Central --- L2
        Central --- L3
        Central --- L4
        Central --- L5
    end
```

The radial topology connects all ligands to a single central ligand. This is also called a "hub and spoke" or "star" topology.

**Function:** `generate_radial_network()`

**Key Parameters:**
- `ligands`: Collection of ligands to arrange around the center
- `central_ligand`: The hub ligand (specified as `SmallMoleculeComponent`, `str` name, or `int` index)
- `mappers`: Atom mapper(s) to use
- `scorer`: Optional scoring function to select best mapping

**Use Cases:**
- When one reference ligand has known experimental data
- Initial exploration of a congeneric series
- Rapid screening with minimal computational cost

**Characteristics:**
- **Edges:** N-1 (where N = number of ligands)
- **Connectivity:** Guaranteed if all ligands can map to center
- **Redundancy:** None - no statistical cross-validation
- **Cost:** Minimal

**Sources:** [openfe/setup/ligand_network_planning.py:49-154](), [openfe/tests/setup/test_network_planning.py:108-317]()

### Minimal Spanning Tree (MST) Network

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "MST Network Topology"
        L1["Ligand 1"]
        L2["Ligand 2"]
        L3["Ligand 3"]
        L4["Ligand 4"]
        L5["Ligand 5"]
        L6["Ligand 6"]
        
        L1 --- L2
        L2 --- L3
        L3 --- L4
        L2 --- L5
        L5 --- L6
    end
```

The MST topology creates a connected network with the minimum number of edges while maximizing the total score (typically structural similarity).

**Function:** `generate_minimal_spanning_network()`

**Key Parameters:**
- `ligands`: Collection of ligands to connect
- `mappers`: Atom mapper(s) to use
- `scorer`: **Required** - scoring function to evaluate mappings

**Algorithm:** Uses Kruskal's algorithm via `MinimalSpanningTreeNetworkGenerator` from konnektor.

**Use Cases:**
- Balanced approach for moderate-sized ligand sets
- When computational budget is limited
- When all ligands are reasonably similar

**Characteristics:**
- **Edges:** N-1 (minimum for connectivity)
- **Connectivity:** Guaranteed if all ligands are reachable
- **Redundancy:** None
- **Cost:** Moderate
- **Score Requirement:** Scorer is mandatory for edge selection

**Sources:** [openfe/setup/ligand_network_planning.py:208-249](), [openfe/tests/setup/test_network_planning.py:368-465]()

### Minimal Redundant Network

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "Redundant MST Network (mst_num=2)"
        L1["Ligand 1"]
        L2["Ligand 2"]
        L3["Ligand 3"]
        L4["Ligand 4"]
        L5["Ligand 5"]
        
        L1 --- L2
        L2 --- L3
        L3 --- L4
        L1 -.2nd MST.- L5
        L5 -.2nd MST.- L4
        L2 -.2nd MST.- L5
    end
```

This topology generates multiple overlapping MSTs to provide statistical redundancy. Each node connects to at least `mst_num` edges.

**Function:** `generate_minimal_redundant_network()`

**Key Parameters:**
- `ligands`: Collection of ligands to connect
- `mappers`: Atom mapper(s) to use
- `scorer`: **Required** - scoring function
- `mst_num`: Number of MSTs to generate (default: 2)

**Algorithm:** Iteratively computes MSTs, removing selected edges before each iteration. Uses `RedundantMinimalSpanningTreeNetworkGenerator`.

**Use Cases:**
- Production-quality free energy calculations
- When statistical validation is required
- Standard recommended approach for publication

**Characteristics:**
- **Edges:** Approximately `mst_num × (N-1)`
- **Connectivity:** Guaranteed
- **Redundancy:** Each node connects to ≥ `mst_num` edges
- **Cost:** Higher, scales with `mst_num`
- **Statistical Power:** Enables cycle closure analysis

**Sources:** [openfe/setup/ligand_network_planning.py:252-303](), [openfe/tests/setup/test_network_planning.py:467-568]()

### Maximal Network

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "Maximal Network Topology"
        L1["Ligand 1"]
        L2["Ligand 2"]
        L3["Ligand 3"]
        L4["Ligand 4"]
        
        L1 --- L2
        L1 --- L3
        L1 --- L4
        L2 --- L3
        L2 --- L4
        L3 --- L4
    end
```

The maximal topology attempts to create all possible pairwise mappings (up to N(N-1)/2 edges).

**Function:** `generate_maximal_network()`

**Key Parameters:**
- `ligands`: Collection of ligands
- `mappers`: Atom mapper(s) to use
- `scorer`: Optional scoring function
- `progress`: Show progress bar (default: True)

**Use Cases:**
- Debugging atom mappers (see which pairs fail)
- Small ligand sets (<10 molecules) where exhaustive comparison is feasible
- Maximum statistical redundancy for critical projects

**Characteristics:**
- **Edges:** Up to N(N-1)/2 (actual count may be lower if some mappers fail)
- **Connectivity:** Guaranteed (if any valid mappings exist)
- **Redundancy:** Maximum - every possible cycle
- **Cost:** Very high, O(N²) transformations

**Sources:** [openfe/setup/ligand_network_planning.py:157-205](), [openfe/tests/setup/test_network_planning.py:319-366]()

---

## Network Topology Comparison

| Topology | Edges | Redundancy | Computational Cost | Statistical Power | Best Use Case |
|----------|-------|------------|-------------------|-------------------|---------------|
| **Radial** | N-1 | None | Minimal | Low | Initial screening, reference-based |
| **MST** | N-1 | None | Moderate | Low | Balanced exploration |
| **Redundant MST** | ~2(N-1) | Medium | High | Medium-High | Production calculations |
| **Maximal** | N(N-1)/2 | Maximum | Very High | Maximum | Small sets, debugging |

**Recommended Default:** Minimal Redundant Network with `mst_num=2` provides the best balance of cost and reliability for most applications.

**Sources:** [openfe/setup/ligand_network_planning.py:49-303]()

---

## Explicit Network Construction

For complete control, networks can be specified explicitly by ligand names or indices.

### By Name

```mermaid
graph TB
    Function["generate_network_from_names()"]
    Input["ligands: list[SmallMoleculeComponent]<br/>mapper: AtomMapper<br/>names: list[tuple[str, str]]"]
    NetworkPlanner["ExplicitNetworkGenerator"]
    Output["LigandNetwork"]
    
    Function --> Input
    Input --> NetworkPlanner
    NetworkPlanner --> Output
```

**Function:** `generate_network_from_names()`

Specify edges as tuples of ligand names:

```python
names = [
    ("benzene", "toluene"),
    ("toluene", "phenol"),
    ("phenol", "anisole")
]
```

**Error Handling:**
- Raises `KeyError` if invalid name requested
- Raises `ValueError` if duplicate names exist

**Sources:** [openfe/setup/ligand_network_planning.py:306-343](), [openfe/tests/setup/test_network_planning.py:570-630]()

### By Index

**Function:** `generate_network_from_indices()`

Specify edges as tuples of integer indices (0-based):

```python
indices = [
    (0, 1),  # First ligand to second
    (1, 2),  # Second to third
    (2, 3)   # Third to fourth
]
```

**Error Handling:**
- Raises `IndexError` if invalid index
- Warns if network is disconnected

**Sources:** [openfe/setup/ligand_network_planning.py:346-378](), [openfe/tests/setup/test_network_planning.py:632-680]()

---

## External Network Formats

OpenFE can import networks from other free energy calculation tools.

### Orion NES Format

```mermaid
graph LR
    OrionFile["Orion .dat file<br/>'name >> name' format"]
    LoadFunction["load_orion_network()"]
    Network["LigandNetwork"]
    
    OrionFile --> LoadFunction
    LoadFunction --> Network
```

**Function:** `load_orion_network()`

**File Format:**
```
# Total number of edges: 3
# ------------------------
benzene >> toluene
toluene >> phenol
phenol >> anisole
```

Lines starting with `#` are comments. Edge lines must follow `name >> name` format.

**Sources:** [openfe/setup/ligand_network_planning.py:381-424](), [openfe/tests/setup/test_network_planning.py:682-756]()

### FEP+ Edges Format

**Function:** `load_fepplus_network()`

**File Format:**
```
hash:hash # benzene -> toluene
hash:hash # toluene -> phenol
hash:hash # phenol -> anisole
```

Each line must follow `hash:hash # name -> name` format.

**Sources:** [openfe/setup/ligand_network_planning.py:427-471](), [openfe/tests/setup/test_network_planning.py:714-778]()

---

## Implementation Details

### Mapper Optimization

The `_hasten_lomap()` helper function optimizes LOMAP mapper performance by pre-computing a common core for all ligands:

```mermaid
graph LR
    Input["LomapAtomMapper<br/>+ ligands"]
    Check{"Has seed<br/>already?"}
    FindCore["_find_common_core()<br/>via LOMAP"]
    NewMapper["LomapAtomMapper<br/>with seed"]
    
    Input --> Check
    Check -->|No| FindCore
    FindCore --> NewMapper
    Check -->|Yes| Return["Return<br/>original"]
```

This reduces redundant MCS calculations when mapping many ligand pairs.

**Sources:** [openfe/setup/ligand_network_planning.py:27-46]()

### Network Generation Flow

```mermaid
graph TB
    UserInput["User specifies:<br/>ligands, mappers, scorer"]
    NetworkPlanner["Konnektor NetworkPlanner<br/>(StarNetworkGenerator,<br/>MinimalSpanningTreeNetworkGenerator,<br/>etc.)"]
    MappingGen["Generate all pairwise<br/>LigandAtomMappings"]
    Scoring["Apply scorer to<br/>rank mappings"]
    GraphAlg["Graph algorithm<br/>(MST, maximal, etc.)"]
    LigandNet["LigandNetwork<br/>with selected edges"]
    
    UserInput --> NetworkPlanner
    NetworkPlanner --> MappingGen
    MappingGen --> Scoring
    Scoring --> GraphAlg
    GraphAlg --> LigandNet
```

All network generation functions delegate to specialized generators from the `konnektor` library:
- `StarNetworkGenerator` for radial networks
- `MinimalSpanningTreeNetworkGenerator` for MST
- `RedundantMinimalSpanningTreeNetworkGenerator` for redundant MST
- `MaximalNetworkGenerator` for maximal networks
- `ExplicitNetworkGenerator` for custom networks

**Sources:** [openfe/setup/ligand_network_planning.py:17-24](), [openfe/setup/ligand_network_planning.py:130-139]()

### Disconnected Node Handling

Network generators check for disconnected nodes after construction:

```mermaid
graph TB
    Generated["Generated<br/>LigandNetwork"]
    Check{"Is connected?"}
    FindComponents["Find weakly<br/>connected components<br/>(NetworkX)"]
    LargestComponent["Identify largest<br/>component"]
    MissingNodes["Calculate<br/>missing_nodes"]
    Error["Raise RuntimeError<br/>listing unreachable nodes"]
    Return["Return<br/>network"]
    
    Generated --> Check
    Check -->|No| FindComponents
    FindComponents --> LargestComponent
    LargestComponent --> MissingNodes
    MissingNodes --> Error
    Check -->|Yes| Return
```

If any ligands cannot be mapped, the function raises `RuntimeError` with the names of unreachable nodes.

**Sources:** [openfe/setup/ligand_network_planning.py:141-152](), [openfe/tests/setup/test_network_planning.py:303-316, 448-464]()

---

## Scorer Integration

Most network generation functions accept an optional `scorer` parameter—a callable that takes a `LigandAtomMapping` and returns a `float`. Higher scores indicate better mappings.

### Scorer Behavior

| Scenario | Behavior |
|----------|----------|
| Single mapper, no scorer | Use first valid mapping |
| Multiple mappers, no scorer | Use first valid mapping from first mapper |
| With scorer | Evaluate all mapper outputs, select highest score |
| MST/Redundant without scorer | **Error** - scorer required for graph algorithms |

**Common Scorers:**
- `default_lomap_score` - LOMAP's composite scoring (see [Atom Mapping](#3.1))
- `default_perses_scorer` - Perses scoring function
- Custom functions based on mapping size, RMSD, etc.

**Sources:** [openfe/setup/ligand_network_planning.py:74-77](), [openfe/tests/setup/test_network_planning.py:40-46, 248-277]()

---

## Error Handling and Validation

### Common Errors

| Error Type | Condition | Example |
|------------|-----------|---------|
| `RuntimeError` | No mapping to central ligand (radial) | Unmappable chemistry to hub |
| `RuntimeError` | Unreachable nodes (MST) | Isolated ligand with no valid mappings |
| `KeyError` | Invalid ligand name | Typo in `generate_network_from_names()` |
| `IndexError` | Invalid ligand index | Out-of-bounds index |
| `ValueError` | Duplicate ligand names | Same name used twice |
| `ValueError` | Central ligand specification error | Multiple ligands with same name, or negative index |

### Warnings

| Warning | Condition | Action |
|---------|-----------|--------|
| `UserWarning` | Central ligand in `ligands` list | Automatically removed to avoid self-edge |
| `UserWarning` | Disconnected network from indices | Network generated but connectivity questionable |

**Sources:** [openfe/tests/setup/test_network_planning.py:181-218, 303-316, 596-629, 656-679]()

---

| `load_fepplus_network()` | [openfe/setup/ligand_network_planning.py:427-471]() | Import from FEP+ |

| Component | Source | Role |
|-----------|--------|------|

# Page: Alchemical Network Planning

# Alchemical Network Planning

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

## Purpose and Scope

This document explains the alchemical network planning system in OpenFE, which is responsible for creating and configuring networks of alchemical transformations for free energy calculations. Alchemical network planning connects the atom mapping system (described in [Atom Mapping](#3.1)) with the simulation protocols (described in [Core Protocols](#2)) by determining which transformations to perform and building the complete alchemical network with the necessary chemical systems and configurations.

The alchemical network planners handle:
1. Coordinating atom mapping between molecules
2. Planning the optimal network of transformations 
3. Generating appropriate chemical systems for each state
4. Configuring protocol settings for each transformation
5. Building the final alchemical network that can be executed

Sources: [openfe/setup/alchemical_network_planner/abstract_alchemical_network_planner.py:1-17](), [openfe/setup/alchemical_network_planner/relative_alchemical_network_planner.py:1-45]()

## Alchemical Network Planner Architecture

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class AbstractAlchemicalNetworkPlanner {
        <<abstract>>
        +__call__() AlchemicalNetwork
    }
    
    class RelativeAlchemicalNetworkPlanner {
        <<abstract>>
        +name: str
        -_mappers: list[LigandAtomMapper]
        -_mapping_scorer: Callable
        -_ligand_network_planner: Callable
        -_protocol: Protocol
        -_chemical_system_generator_type: Type
        +__init__(name, mappers, mapping_scorer, ligand_network_planner, protocol)
        +__call__() AlchemicalNetwork
        +mappers() Iterable[LigandAtomMapper]
        +mapping_scorer() Callable
        +ligand_network_planner() Callable
        +transformation_protocol() Protocol
        +chemical_system_generator_type() Type
        -_construct_ligand_network() LigandNetwork
        -_build_transformations() AlchemicalNetwork
        -_build_transformation() Transformation
    }
    
    class RHFEAlchemicalNetworkPlanner {
        +__init__(name, mappers, mapping_scorer, ligand_network_planner, protocol)
        +__call__(ligands, solvent) AlchemicalNetwork
    }
    
    class RBFEAlchemicalNetworkPlanner {
        +__init__(name, mappers, mapping_scorer, ligand_network_planner, protocol)
        +__call__(ligands, solvent, protein, cofactors) AlchemicalNetwork
        -_build_transformation() Transformation
    }
    
    AbstractAlchemicalNetworkPlanner <|-- RelativeAlchemicalNetworkPlanner
    RelativeAlchemicalNetworkPlanner <|-- RHFEAlchemicalNetworkPlanner
    RelativeAlchemicalNetworkPlanner <|-- RBFEAlchemicalNetworkPlanner
```

**Diagram: Hierarchy of Alchemical Network Planners**

The alchemical network planning system follows a hierarchical design with specialized planners for different types of free energy calculations:

1. **AbstractAlchemicalNetworkPlanner**: The base abstract class that defines the interface for all network planners.
   
2. **RelativeAlchemicalNetworkPlanner**: An abstract implementation that handles the common logic for relative free energy calculations (both hydration and binding).
   
3. **RHFEAlchemicalNetworkPlanner**: A concrete implementation for Relative Hydration Free Energy (RHFE) calculations, which involve transformations between molecules in vacuum and solvent.
   
4. **RBFEAlchemicalNetworkPlanner**: A concrete implementation for Relative Binding Free Energy (RBFE) calculations, which involve transformations between molecules bound to a protein in solvent.

Each planner is responsible for coordinating the creation of appropriate chemical systems and transformations based on the specific type of free energy calculation.

Sources: [openfe/setup/alchemical_network_planner/abstract_alchemical_network_planner.py:1-17](), [openfe/setup/alchemical_network_planner/relative_alchemical_network_planner.py:46-120](), [openfe/setup/alchemical_network_planner/relative_alchemical_network_planner.py:233-294](), [openfe/setup/alchemical_network_planner/relative_alchemical_network_planner.py:296-403]()

## Network Planning Process

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph "Input Components"
        SM["SmallMoleculeComponents"]
        PR["ProteinComponent (for RBFE)"]
        SV["SolventComponent"]
        CF["Cofactors (optional)"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Ligand Network Planning"
        AM["Atom Mapping"]
        SC["Mapping Scoring"]
        NP["Network Planning Strategy"]
        LN["Ligand Network"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Chemical System Generation"
        VA["Vacuum Systems"]
        SO["Solvent Systems"]
        CO["Complex Systems"]
        CS["Chemical Systems"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Transformation Building"
        PS["Protocol Settings"]
        TR["Transformations"]
        AN["Alchemical Network"]
    end
    
    SM --> AM
    AM --> SC
    SC --> NP
    NP --> LN
    
    SM --> VA
    SM --> SO
    SM --> CO
    PR --> CO
    SV --> SO
    SV --> CO
    CF --> CO
    
    VA --> CS
    SO --> CS
    CO --> CS
    
    LN --> TR
    CS --> TR
    PS --> TR
    TR --> AN
```

**Diagram: Alchemical Network Planning Process Flow**

The alchemical network planning process follows a series of defined steps:

1. **Input Preparation**:
   - Small molecules for transformation
   - Protein component (for binding calculations)
   - Solvent component
   - Optional cofactors

2. **Ligand Network Construction**:
   - Generate atom mappings between molecule pairs using `LigandAtomMapper` implementations
   - Score mappings using a mapping scorer function (typically the default LOMAP scorer)
   - Plan the network using a network planner function (typically generating a minimal spanning tree)
   - Create a `LigandNetwork` containing the planned transformations

3. **Chemical System Generation**:
   - Create appropriate chemical systems for each environment:
     - Vacuum systems (for RHFE)
     - Solvent systems (for both RHFE and RBFE)
     - Complex systems with protein (for RBFE)
   - Include any cofactors in complex systems if provided

4. **Transformation Building**:
   - Create transformations for each edge in the ligand network
   - Configure protocol settings based on transformation type
   - Handle special cases (e.g., charge-changing transformations)
   - Construct the final alchemical network

Sources: [openfe/setup/alchemical_network_planner/relative_alchemical_network_planner.py:121-191](), [openfe/setup/alchemical_network_planner/relative_alchemical_network_planner.py:192-232]()

## Chemical System Generation

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class AbstractChemicalSystemGenerator {
        <<abstract>>
        +__call__() Iterable[ChemicalSystem]
    }
    
    class EasyChemicalSystemGenerator {
        +solvent: SolventComponent
        +protein: ProteinComponent
        +cofactors: list[SmallMoleculeComponent]
        +do_vacuum: bool
        +__init__(solvent, protein, cofactors, do_vacuum)
        +__call__(component) Iterable[ChemicalSystem]
    }
    
    class RFEComponentLabels {
        <<enumeration>>
        +PROTEIN: "protein"
        +LIGAND: "ligand"
        +SOLVENT: "solvent"
        +COFACTOR: "cofactor"
    }
    
    AbstractChemicalSystemGenerator <|-- EasyChemicalSystemGenerator
    EasyChemicalSystemGenerator -- RFEComponentLabels
```

**Diagram: Chemical System Generation Architecture**

A critical part of alchemical network planning is the generation of chemical systems for each transformation. This is handled by the `EasyChemicalSystemGenerator` class, which creates chemical systems with consistent components based on the type of free energy calculation:

1. **Chemical System Environment Types**:
   - **Vacuum**: Just the small molecule in vacuum (for RHFE vacuum leg)
   - **Solvent**: Small molecule in solvent (for both RHFE and RBFE solvent legs)
   - **Complex**: Small molecule bound to protein in solvent (for RBFE complex leg)

2. **Component Labeling**:
   - Components in chemical systems are labeled using the `RFEComponentLabels` enumeration:
     - `LIGAND`: The small molecule being transformed
     - `PROTEIN`: The protein component (for RBFE)
     - `SOLVENT`: The solvent component
     - `COFACTOR`: Any cofactors in the system (numbered from 1)

3. **System Generation Process**:
   - The generator is initialized with the environment components (solvent, protein, cofactors)
   - When called with a small molecule component, it yields chemical systems for each relevant environment
   - Systems are named based on the small molecule name and environment (e.g., `"ligand_23_vacuum"`, `"ligand_23_solvent"`, `"ligand_23_complex"`)

The chemical system generator ensures that all chemical systems are created with consistent components and naming, which is essential for properly setting up and analyzing free energy calculations.

Sources: [openfe/setup/chemicalsystem_generator/abstract_chemicalsystem_generator.py:1-26](), [openfe/setup/chemicalsystem_generator/easy_chemicalsystem_generator.py:1-124]()

## RHFE vs RBFE Network Planning

### RHFE Network Planning

The `RHFEAlchemicalNetworkPlanner` creates networks for relative hydration free energy calculations, which involve:

1. **Transformations Between Small Molecules**:
   - In vacuum (small molecule only)
   - In solvent (small molecule in solvent)

2. **Workflow**:
   - Create atom mappings between all pairs of small molecules
   - Score mappings and plan the optimal network
   - Generate vacuum and solvent chemical systems for each small molecule
   - Build transformations between corresponding systems

### RBFE Network Planning

The `RBFEAlchemicalNetworkPlanner` creates networks for relative binding free energy calculations, which involve:

1. **Transformations Between Small Molecules**:
   - In solvent (small molecule in solvent)
   - In complex (small molecule bound to protein in solvent)

2. **Workflow**:
   - Create atom mappings between all pairs of small molecules
   - Score mappings and plan the optimal network
   - Generate solvent and complex chemical systems for each small molecule
   - Build transformations between corresponding systems
   - Handle special cases like charge-changing transformations

### Special Handling for Charge Changes

The `RBFEAlchemicalNetworkPlanner` includes special handling for transformations where the net charge changes between the two small molecules:

```python
# If the transformation involves a charge change, apply special settings
if get_alchemical_charge_difference(ligand_mapping_edge) != 0:
    # Issue a warning
    warnings.warn("Charge changing transformation between ligands...")
    
    # Apply more rigorous simulation settings
    protocol_settings.alchemical_settings.explicit_charge_correction = True
    protocol_settings.simulation_settings.production_length = 20 * unit.nanosecond
    protocol_settings.simulation_settings.n_replicas = 22
    protocol_settings.lambda_settings.lambda_windows = 22
```

These special settings ensure more accurate results for charge-changing transformations, which are typically more challenging.

Sources: [openfe/setup/alchemical_network_planner/relative_alchemical_network_planner.py:233-294](), [openfe/setup/alchemical_network_planner/relative_alchemical_network_planner.py:296-403](), [openfe/setup/alchemical_network_planner/relative_alchemical_network_planner.py:320-358]()

## Command Line Interface

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph "Input Files and Options"
        SM["Small Molecule Files"]
        PR["Protein File (RBFE only)"]
        CF["Cofactor Files (optional)"]
        YA["YAML Settings File"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Network Planning Commands"
        RBFE["plan-rbfe-network"]
        RHFE["plan-rhfe-network"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Network Planning Implementation"
        PCG["Partial Charge Generation"]
        ANP["Alchemical Network Planning"]
        LNP["Ligand Network Planning"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Output Files"
        AN["alchemicalNetwork.json"]
        LN["ligandNetwork.json"]
        TF["Transformation JSON Files"]
    end
    
    SM --> RBFE
    PR --> RBFE
    CF --> RBFE
    YA --> RBFE
    
    SM --> RHFE
    YA --> RHFE
    
    RBFE --> PCG
    RHFE --> PCG
    
    PCG --> ANP
    ANP --> LNP
    
    ANP --> AN
    LNP --> LN
    ANP --> TF
```

**Diagram: Command Line Interface for Network Planning**

OpenFE provides two main command line tools for alchemical network planning:

1. **plan-rbfe-network**: For planning relative binding free energy calculations
   - Requires small molecule files, protein file, and optional cofactor files
   - Creates an alchemical network with transformations in solvent and complex environments

2. **plan-rhfe-network**: For planning relative hydration free energy calculations
   - Requires only small molecule files
   - Creates an alchemical network with transformations in vacuum and solvent environments

Both commands share common features:

1. **Partial Charge Generation**:
   - Automatically assigns partial charges to small molecules if not already present
   - Can be customized using the YAML settings file
   - Can optionally overwrite existing charges with `--overwrite-charges`

2. **Network Planning Configuration**:
   - Atom mapping method (default: LOMAP)
   - Mapping scoring function (default: LOMAP default scorer)
   - Network planning strategy (default: minimal spanning network)
   - Protocol settings (default: RelativeHybridTopologyProtocol with standard settings)

3. **Output**:
   - Alchemical network JSON file
   - Ligand network JSON file
   - Individual transformation JSON files for each edge in the network
   - These files can be used with the `quickrun` command to execute simulations

### Example Command Usage

```
# RBFE Planning
openfe plan-rbfe-network -M molecules_directory -p protein.pdb -o output_directory -s settings.yaml

# RHFE Planning
openfe plan-rhfe-network -M molecules_directory -o output_directory -s settings.yaml
```

Sources: [openfecli/commands/plan_rbfe_network.py:1-265](), [openfecli/commands/plan_rhfe_network.py:1-219](), [openfecli/tests/commands/test_plan_rbfe_network.py:1-424](), [openfecli/tests/commands/test_plan_rhfe_network.py:1-242]()

## YAML Configuration Options

The behavior of the alchemical network planners can be customized through a YAML configuration file:

```yaml
# Network planning strategy
network:
  method: generate_minimal_spanning_network  # or generate_lomap_network, generate_radial_network, etc.
  settings:
    # Strategy-specific settings
    # e.g., max_path_length: 6 for LOMAP network

# Atom mapping method
mapper:
  method: LomapAtomMapper
  settings:
    time: 45
    element_change: True
    # Other mapper-specific settings

# Partial charge method
partial_charge:
  method: am1bcc  # or nagl, mmff, etc.
  settings:
    # Method-specific settings
    # e.g., nagl_model: "openff-gnn-am1bcc-0.1.0-rc.3.pt" for nagl
```

This configuration system allows for flexible customization of the network planning process, including:

1. **Network Planning Strategy**:
   - `generate_minimal_spanning_network`: Creates a minimal spanning tree (default)
   - `generate_lomap_network`: Uses LOMAP's network planning algorithm
   - `generate_radial_network`: Creates a hub-and-spoke network from a central ligand

2. **Atom Mapping Method**:
   - `LomapAtomMapper`: Uses LOMAP for atom mapping (with customizable parameters)
   - Other mappers as implemented in the system

3. **Partial Charge Method**:
   - `am1bcc`: Uses AM1-BCC charges (default)
   - `nagl`: Uses neural network-based charge assignment
   - `mmff`: Uses MMFF94 charges
   - Others as supported by the charge generation system

Sources: [openfecli/tests/commands/test_plan_rbfe_network.py:337-354](), [openfecli/tests/commands/test_plan_rbfe_network.py:381-398](), [openfecli/tests/commands/test_plan_rhfe_network.py:162-179]()

## Programmatic Usage

For advanced use cases, the alchemical network planners can be used directly in Python code:

```python
# RBFE Planning
from openfe.setup.alchemical_network_planner import RBFEAlchemicalNetworkPlanner
from openfe.setup import LomapAtomMapper, lomap_scorers, ligand_network_planning
from openfe.protocols.openmm_rfe.equil_rfe_methods import RelativeHybridTopologyProtocol

# Create the planner
planner = RBFEAlchemicalNetworkPlanner(
    mappers=[LomapAtomMapper()],
    mapping_scorer=lomap_scorers.default_lomap_score,
    ligand_network_planner=ligand_network_planning.generate_minimal_spanning_network,
    protocol=RelativeHybridTopologyProtocol(RelativeHybridTopologyProtocol.default_settings())
)

# Plan the network
alchemical_network = planner(
    ligands=small_molecules,
    solvent=solvent_component,
    protein=protein_component,
    cofactors=[]
)
```

This approach allows for more fine-grained control over the network planning process and integration with other parts of the OpenFE framework.

Sources: [openfecli/commands/plan_rbfe_network.py:11-105](), [openfecli/commands/plan_rhfe_network.py:14-80]()

## Integration with Other Systems

The alchemical network planning system integrates with several other components of the OpenFE framework:

1. **Atom Mapping System** ([Atom Mapping](#3.1)):
   - Uses atom mappers to determine how atoms correspond between molecules
   - Relies on scoring functions to evaluate mapping quality
   - Feeds into network planning strategies to determine optimal transformations

2. **Chemical System Generation**:
   - Creates consistent chemical systems for different environments
   - Ensures correct labeling of components for protocols to identify

3. **Protocols** ([Core Protocols](#2)):
   - Configures protocol settings based on transformation type
   - Handles special cases like charge-changing transformations
   - Creates transformations that can be executed by simulation protocols

4. **Command Line Interface** ([Command Line Interface](#4)):
   - Provides user-friendly tools for common network planning tasks
   - Handles file I/O and configuration management
   - Integrates with simulation execution (`quickrun`) and analysis

This integration allows the alchemical network planning system to serve as a bridge between the input specification and the executable simulation plan.

Sources: [openfe/setup/alchemical_network_planner/relative_alchemical_network_planner.py:1-45](), [openfe/setup/alchemical_network_planner/relative_alchemical_network_planner.py:121-191]()

## Purpose and Scope

This page documents the partial charge generation system in OpenFE, which assigns atomic partial charges to small molecules prior to simulation. Partial charges are essential for non-bonded electrostatic interactions in molecular dynamics and free energy calculations. The system supports multiple charge assignment methods (AM1-BCC, NAGL, Espaloma) and toolkit backends (AmberTools, OpenEye, RDKit), with automatic conformer generation and parallel processing capabilities.

For information about force field settings and system parameterization, see [Protocol Settings and Configuration](#2.5). For network planning workflows that utilize charge generation, see [Alchemical Network Planning](#3.3).

---

## System Architecture

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "User Interface"
        CLI["CLI: charge-molecules<br/>openfecli.commands.generate_partial_charges"]
        PythonAPI["Python API:<br/>bulk_assign_partial_charges()<br/>assign_offmol_partial_charges()"]
        NetworkPlanners["Network Planning Commands:<br/>plan-rbfe-network<br/>plan-rhfe-network"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Core Charge Generation"
        BulkAssign["bulk_assign_partial_charges()<br/>openfe/protocols/openmm_utils/charge_generation.py:434-521"]

        ConfGen["_generate_offmol_conformers()<br/>openfe/protocols/openmm_utils/charge_generation.py:206-282"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Charge Methods"
        AM1BCC["assign_offmol_am1bcc_charges()<br/>am1bcc / am1bccelf10"]

        Espaloma["assign_offmol_espaloma_charges()<br/>espaloma method"]
    end

    end

        YAMLSettings["YAML Settings File<br/>partial_charge section"]

    end
```
